subject: Working with designers and trade partners
hook: One arrow on a cutting list decides how a woodgrain kitchen looks
ig:
One arrow on a cutting list decides how a woodgrain kitchen looks.

For trade customers sending us parts to cut: on plain colours, a 600 × 400 part can be cut either way round on the board. On woodgrain and oak-effect decors, it can't.

If grain direction isn't marked, a door can come off the saw at the correct size but with the grain running across instead of up. On its own it looks odd. In a run of doors, it's obvious.

The simple fix:
- Put the grain-direction dimension first, and say so on the list
- Or mark an arrow or a 'G' against the grain dimension for each woodgrain part
- Flag any parts that need grain continuity, such as a bank of drawer fronts

It also helps us nest the parts on the board efficiently.

Send this to whoever writes your cutting lists. DM us if you want a template layout.
fb:
A small one for the designers and fitters who send us cutting lists: always mark the grain.

On plain decors we can rotate parts on the board to suit. On woodgrain and oak-effect boards we can't, because a door with sideways grain stands out a mile in a run. Put the grain dimension first or add an arrow against it, and flag any parts that need to line up, like stacked drawer fronts.

It saves remakes and helps us get the most out of each sheet. More on our panel cutting service here:
